article.title: Why Correlation Drift Matters Even When Accuracy Looks Stable
article.why: 把 drift 從單變量分布延伸到變數關係與 subgroup，適合模型監控與風險治理。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A machine-learning model can keep the same overall accuracy while its behavior becomes less reliable. One reason is correlation drift: relationships among input variables, outcomes, and subgroups can change even when simple averages look stable. Monitoring only headline performance may therefore miss an important structural shift.

Imagine a model that predicts which customers are likely to respond to an offer. During training, recent website visits and high account balances may both be associated with conversion. Six months later, the average number of website visits and the average balance in the scoring population may be almost unchanged. Yet the relationship between those variables and conversion may have shifted. Perhaps a new campaign attracts many curious visitors who browse frequently but rarely buy. The marginal distributions look stable, but the predictive relationship has weakened.

This is different from simple feature drift. Feature drift asks whether the distribution of an input changed. Correlation drift asks whether variables still move together in the same way or retain the same relationship with the target. A model can therefore pass several univariate drift checks while the joint structure changes underneath it.

Why does this matter if accuracy is still acceptable? First, aggregate accuracy can hide subgroup deterioration. Performance may improve for one segment and worsen for another, producing little change in the total. Second, labels may arrive slowly. A credit, fraud, retention, or marketing model can operate for weeks before true outcomes are fully observed. Structural drift can provide an earlier warning than delayed performance metrics.

Teams can monitor this in several ways. They can compare correlation matrices over time, examine pairwise relationships among important features, track feature-target associations once labels arrive, and monitor model explanations or feature contributions by segment. For nonlinear models, simple Pearson correlation is not enough, so teams may use rank correlation, mutual-information measures, partial dependence, or carefully chosen business diagnostics.

However, more monitoring is not automatically better. A large feature set can produce thousands of pairwise statistics and many false alarms. The objective is not to detect every numerical change. It is to identify changes that could alter decisions. Monitoring should therefore focus on variables that materially influence model outputs, high-risk segments, and relationships that have a clear business interpretation.

Correlation drift also matters when a model is retrained frequently. Automatic retraining can adapt to new patterns, but it can also hide why the environment changed. If a relationship disappears because customer behavior changed, that is a business insight, not merely a modeling problem. Teams should record important structural shifts and ask whether product design, pricing, policy, data collection, or external conditions changed.

A practical monitoring framework can have three layers. The first checks input distributions. The second checks joint structure and subgroup behavior. The third checks outcome performance when labels become available. Alerts should be linked to actions: investigate data quality, review a segment, recalibrate a threshold, retrain the model, or pause automated decisions.

The broader lesson is that stability is multidimensional. Stable averages do not guarantee stable relationships, and stable aggregate accuracy does not guarantee stable behavior. A mature monitoring process asks not only whether the inputs look similar and whether the final metric is acceptable, but also whether the model is still relying on relationships that make sense in the current environment.

For governance, this distinction improves diagnosis. If a metric moves, the team can determine whether the cause is population change, relationship change, labeling delay, or true model degradation instead of treating every alert as the same failure.
paragraphs.zh:
機器學習模型即使整體 accuracy 維持不變，行為仍可能變得不可靠。其中一個原因是 correlation drift：輸入變數、結果與 subgroup 之間的關係可能改變，即使簡單平均值看起來穩定。只監控 headline performance 因此可能漏掉重要的結構性變化。

例如一個預測客戶是否會回應行銷的模型，訓練時網站造訪次數與高帳戶餘額都和 conversion 有關。六個月後，這兩個變數的平均值幾乎沒變，但它們與 conversion 的關係可能已經改變。新活動也許吸引很多常瀏覽卻不購買的人。邊際分布穩定，不代表 predictive relationship 穩定。

這和單純 feature drift 不同。Feature drift 問的是某個輸入的分布是否改變；correlation drift 問的是變數彼此之間、或與 target 之間的關係是否仍相同。因此模型可以通過多個單變量 drift 檢查，但 joint structure 已經改變。

即使 accuracy 還能接受也必須在意。第一，aggregate accuracy 可能掩蓋 subgroup deterioration，一個 segment 變好、另一個變差，總體看起來沒有明顯變化。第二，label 常常延遲，信用、詐欺、留存或行銷模型可能運作數週後才拿到完整 outcome。Structural drift 有機會比延遲的 performance metric 更早發出警訊。

監控方法包括比較不同時間的 correlation matrix、檢查重要特徵的 pairwise relationship、label 到齊後追蹤 feature-target association，以及分 segment 監控 model explanation 或 feature contribution。非線性模型不能只靠 Pearson correlation，也可使用 rank correlation、mutual information、partial dependence 或有業務意義的診斷。

但監控越多並不一定越好。大量特徵會產生數千個 pairwise statistics 與大量 false alarm。目的不是捕捉每個數值變化，而是找出可能改變決策的變化。因此應優先看真正影響輸出的變數、高風險 segment，以及能被業務解釋的關係。

頻繁 retrain 的模型也要注意 correlation drift。自動 retraining 能適應新 pattern，卻可能掩蓋環境為什麼改變。如果某個關係消失是因為客戶行為改變，那不只是 modeling issue，也是 business insight。應記錄重要 structural shift，並檢查產品、價格、政策、資料蒐集或外部條件是否改變。

實務監控可分三層：第一層看輸入分布；第二層看 joint structure 與 subgroup；第三層在 label 到齊後看 outcome performance。Alert 必須連結具體 action，例如查資料品質、review segment、recalibrate threshold、retrain 或暫停自動決策。

核心觀念是 stability 有很多面向。平均值穩定不代表關係穩定，整體 accuracy 穩定也不代表所有行為穩定。成熟監控除了問輸入是否相似、最終 metric 是否可接受，也要問模型現在依賴的關係是否仍符合目前環境。

治理上，這能提升診斷能力：metric 移動時，可區分 population change、relationship change、label delay 或真正 model degradation，而不是把所有 alert 都當成同一種失敗。
paragraphs.ja:
機械学習モデルはoverall accuracyが同じでも、挙動の信頼性が低下することがあります。原因の一つがcorrelation driftです。入力変数、outcome、subgroup間の関係は、平均値が安定していても変化します。headline performanceだけでは構造変化を見逃す可能性があります。

例えば顧客のoffer responseを予測するモデルで、学習時にはwebsite visitsとaccount balanceがconversionと関連していたとします。半年後、両変数の平均はほぼ同じでも、conversionとの関係が変わることがあります。新campaignが閲覧は多いが購入しない人を集めれば、marginal distributionは安定していてもpredictive relationshipは弱くなります。

Feature driftは入力分布が変わったかを見ますが、correlation driftは変数同士やtargetとの関係が同じかを見ます。そのため複数のunivariate drift checkを通過してもjoint structureが変化している場合があります。

Accuracyが許容範囲でも重要です。aggregate accuracyはsubgroup deteriorationを隠すことがあります。またlabel到着が遅い業務では、真のperformanceを確認する前に数週間運用されます。structural driftは早期警告になる可能性があります。

監視ではcorrelation matrix、重要feature間のpairwise relationship、label取得後のfeature-target association、segment別feature contributionなどを比較します。非線形モデルではPearson correlationだけでなくrank correlation、mutual information、partial dependenceやbusiness diagnosticも使えます。

ただし監視項目を増やしすぎるとfalse alarmが増えます。すべての数値変化を検知するのではなく、意思決定を変える可能性がある変化へ集中するべきです。重要feature、高risk segment、業務解釈できる関係を優先します。

頻繁なretrainingでもcorrelation driftは重要です。自動再学習は適応できますが、なぜ環境が変わったかを隠すことがあります。顧客行動変化ならmodeling problemだけでなくbusiness insightです。

実務では三層に分けられます。入力分布、joint structureとsubgroup、label取得後のoutcome performanceです。alertはdata quality確認、segment review、threshold recalibration、retraining、automation停止などのactionへ結びつけます。

Stabilityは多面的です。平均が安定しても関係は安定せず、aggregate accuracyが安定しても全segmentが安定するとは限りません。現在の環境でモデルが依存する関係がまだ妥当かまで確認する必要があります。

Governance上も、population change、relationship change、label delay、true model degradationを区別できれば、すべてのalertを同じfailureとして扱わずに済みます。

quiz.question: How is correlation drift different from feature drift?
quiz.answer: Feature drift concerns an input distribution; correlation drift concerns relationships among variables or with the target.

quiz.question: Why can stable aggregate accuracy be misleading?
quiz.answer: Different subgroups can improve and deteriorate at the same time.

quiz.question: Output: Name one monitoring action after a structural drift alert.
quiz.answer: Example: review the affected segment or recalibrate a threshold.
